title: Count of Substrings Containing Every Vowel and K Consonants I
statement: A substring is a non-empty run of consecutive characters of `word`. Count the substrings in which each of the five vowels `a`, `e`, `i`, `o` and `u` shows up at least once and which hold exactly `k` consonants, where a consonant is any letter other than those five and repeated consonants are counted every time they occur. Return that count. Substrings at different positions are counted separately, even when they spell the same text.
constraints: word contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every substring works for 250 characters; a sliding window does it in linear time. "Exactly `k` consonants" is awkward for one window: for a fixed end, the starts that give exactly `k` consonants form a range in the middle, not a prefix. "At least" conditions behave better: if `word[start..right]` has all five vowels and at least `need` consonants, so does every substring that starts further left and ends at `right`. So for each `right`, the good starts are `0, 1, ..., left - 1` for a `left` that only moves forward. Counting "at least `k`" and subtracting "at least `k + 1`" leaves exactly `k`.

## Approach

1. `atLeast(need)` counts substrings with all five vowels and at least `need` consonants.
2. Move `right` across `word`. A vowel goes into `vowelCount` (vowel to occurrences in the window); a consonant increases `consonants`.
3. While `word[left..right]` still has all five vowels and at least `need` consonants, take `word[left]` out of the window and move `left` forward.
4. Now every start before `left` makes a good substring ending at `right`, so add `left` to `total`.
5. Return `atLeast(k) - atLeast(k + 1)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "aeioqq"`, `k = 1`. There is no `u`, so `vowelCount` never reaches five keys, the while loop never runs and `left` stays 0. `atLeast(1)` and `atLeast(2)` both return 0, and the answer is `0 - 0 = 0`. On Example 2 (`"aeiou"`, `k = 0`), `atLeast(0)` drops the `a` at `right = 4` and counts 1, while `atLeast(1)` counts 0, so the answer is 1.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): in each call `right` and `left` each move forward at most n times.
- Space: O(1): `vowelCount` holds at most five keys.

## Pitfalls

- "Exactly `k`" does not stay true as a substring grows, so one shrinking window cannot count it; subtract two "at least" counts instead.
- Consonants are counted with repeats: `"qq"` is two consonants.
- Add `left` on every step, even when the loop did not move it: the starts before it stay good as `right` grows.
- Delete a vowel from the map when its count drops to 0, or `vowelCount.size` claims vowels that are gone.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `atLeast(need)` | substrings with all five vowels and at least `need` consonants |
| `vowelCount` | each vowel in the window and how often it occurs |
| `consonants` | consonants in the window `word[left..right]` |
| `left`, `right` | first and last index of the window |
| `ch`, `gone` | the character entering and the one leaving the window |
| `total` | good substrings counted so far in this call |

narration.9: Grow the window by one character on the right.
narration.12: A vowel: count one more occurrence of it in the window.
narration.14: Any other letter is a consonant, so the window holds one more.
narration.16: While the window still has all five vowels and enough consonants, a later start might also work, so shrink.
narration.17: The character at left is about to leave the window.
narration.19: A vowel leaves: lower its count.
narration.21: No copy of that vowel is left, so drop it and keep the map size equal to the distinct vowels present.
narration.26: Move the start one step right.
narration.28: Every start from 0 to left - 1 gives a good substring ending at right.
narration.30: All ends have been counted for this threshold.
narration.33: Exactly k consonants is at least k minus at least k + 1.
